output.public_justification: Certification can be defended only on a narrow, qualified basis. A prior approval of the same model family provides contextual continuity, but it does not by itself cover the current retrieval configuration change or current evaluation batch. Because no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is attached, the strongest supportable certification position is that certification proceeds only with explicit current-release documentation of this subgroup weakness and associated limitation in the model-card materials.

It is a narrow, caveated certification case grounded in current admissible evidence: the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.1 percentage points, shows no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and is consistent with public governance principles favoring transparent documentation of limitations and ongoing risk monitoring. The limiting fact is the current small-business onboarding regression, which the record shows is 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold. Because the policy allows certification only when current results are reflected and material weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation, the strongest defensible position is certification only if the current-release model-card materials explicitly disclose that subgroup weakness and associated limitation.
